articles.title: Ramis: "Los pies en el suelo y a la luna, si tenemos que ir de viaje, que sea en la jornada 38"
articles.standfirst: "El equipo quiere, tiene alma y es inteligente", aseguró el entrenador de Osasuna tras la victoria ante el Getafe
articles.summary: "El equipo quiere, tiene alma y es inteligente", aseguró el entrenador de Osasuna tras la victoria ante el Getafe
articles.body: El entrenador de Osasuna, Luis Miguel Ramis, destacó, tras la victoria por 1-0 ante el Getafe en El Sadar, el carácter y la capacidad de sus jugadores para interpretar los partidos y aseguró que "el equipo quiere, tiene alma, tiene carácter y es inteligente a nivel colectivo". Ramis se mostró satisfecho con los siete puntos sumados por Osasuna en las tres primeras jornadas, disputadas en apenas ocho días, y especialmente con la respuesta de sus futbolistas ante una semana que calificó de "muy exigente" en el apartado físico. "Lo más importante es que el equipo entiende lo que queremos de ellos y en cada partido ha interpretado muy bien lo que hace", señaló el técnico, quien considera que los resultados están premiando "la constancia y la voluntad de los jugadores para hacer las cosas bien". Sobre el encuentro ante el Getafe, Ramis explicó que una de las claves fue "ponerle mucha alma al partido", algo que también percibió desde la grada. Osasuna, añadió, supo mantener el orden y defender ante la exigencia física y el juego directo del conjunto madrileño. El entrenador rojillo explicó que su equipo ha evitado realizar una presión demasiado adelantada ante un rival que buscaba superar líneas mediante balones largos y cargar posteriormente las zonas de segunda jugada. "Era absurdo saltar con jugadores porque luego ibas a tener que ir para atrás", apuntó. Ramis diferenció además entre una primera parte en la que Osasuna buscó tener más el balón y controlar el encuentro y una segunda en la que el cansancio obligó a los rojillos a "protegerse" más defensivamente y buscar las transiciones. "Cuando el cuerpo no te da lo mejor o te quedas sin energía, lo mejor es refugiarse, juntarse y ponerle dificultades" al rival, señaló el técnico, quien valoró especialmente que el Getafe no haya generado suficientes ocasiones pese a su fortaleza física y su capacidad para cargar el área. El entrenador también subrayó la solidez defensiva mostrada en este inicio liguero, en el que Osasuna ha encajado un solo gol en tres jornadas. "Esa es la línea", afirmó Ramis, quien quiere que los goles que reciba su equipo sean consecuencia de los méritos del rival y no de una mala organización propia. En cuanto a las lesiones, Ramis explicó que Jorge Herrando presenta un problema muscular en el aductor y Aimar Oroz unas molestias en los isquiotibiales. El técnico señaló que la lesión de Herrando "parece más importante" que la de Aimar, aunque pidió esperar a las pruebas médicas para conocer su alcance. Ramis insistió, no obstante, en su confianza en toda la plantilla. "Si uno no está, aparecerán los otros", afirmó antes de citar diferentes alternativas para suplir posibles bajas. Sobre la clasificación después de sumar siete puntos de nueve posibles, rechazó extraer conclusiones a estas alturas del campeonato. "Los pies en el suelo y a la luna, si tenemos que ir de viaje, que sea en la jornada 38, en la tres no me atrevo", dijo. Finalmente, sobre las últimas horas del mercado de fichajes, Ramis apuntó que todavía puede producirse alguna incorporación y que no espera salidas. "Creo que alguna incorporación va a haber más", señaló, aunque advirtió de que los últimos días de mercado pueden generar operaciones inesperadas

articles.title: Messi, the immigrant who never forgot his homeland
articles.summary: How Lionel Messi remained rooted in his Argentine heritage throughout a career that redefined global soccer and modern sports history.
articles.body: Everything around him was chaos. Red jerseys moved through the chaos, converging in embraces of euphoria and glory. Tears and anger led his teammates to turn what had been a sporting contest into a battle once the match was over. The stadium music blended with the victorious fans’ shouts of jubilation and the losing side’s songs of pride and gratitude. His gaze remained fixed on the stands most crowded with his compatriots. Some claimed he turned his back on the award ceremony out of anger. In reality, Lionel Messi was trying to imprint every image on his memory, to hold onto every sound, every feeling. He wanted to absorb it all, knowing that moment would serve as the raw material for the countless times he would remember this day. He was sad for having lost the World Cup Final, but he wept inconsolably because he knew it was his final match with the Argentina National Team. Messi is an immigrant who left his homeland as a child to seek better opportunities for himself and his family, just like millions of people who leave their native countries every day. And like most migrants, he never forgot his love for his country. He could have chosen to represent Spain instead of Argentina, a decision that likely would have earned him three or four World Cup titles. Yet he never denied his roots. Beyond his immense talent, his humility and respect in a foreign land are key reasons why he remains a global Latin American icon.. The greatest soccer player in history spent only the first 13 years of his life in Rosario. His origin story is well known: diagnosed with a growth hormone deficiency, he required costly treatment that his family could not afford and his local club refused to cover. FC Barcelona stepped in to pay for the medical care. The economic situation in Argentina, as across much of the region, remains complex, often leaving the airport as the only viable path forward. In the youth divisions of the Catalan club, he immediately stood out. Soon, efforts began to have “La Pulga (the flea),” as he was nicknamed at the time, play for the Spanish national team. But his and his family’s attachment to their roots was very strong. Even as a child, he stated in an interview that his dream was “to play for the Argentina national team.” Acting fast, the Argentine Football Association organized a friendly match to debut Messi for their under-20 squad and be “locked in.” That’s how his journey began, on June 29, 2004, just days after he turned 17. Argentine fans were eager to see him play for the senior national team. That moment came on August 17, 2005, in a friendly against Hungary. Incredibly, Messi came on 19 minutes into the second half and was unjustly sent off just seconds later. Perhaps it was a chaotic sign that his path to international glory would not be easy. It is worth taking a brief look back to understand the magnitude of Messi’s legend in the sky blue and white jersey. His journey followed the “hero’s path” of any good movie script. From the mud to the sky. His debut came in the midst of an era full of disappointments and frustrations in Argentina. The country was locked in a constant search to find the “New Maradona” to restore national glory. To make matters worse, Messi was left-footed, wore the number 10 and dazzled everyone. The comparison was as inevitable as it was unfair, placing immense pressure on his shoulder. While he was winning absolutely everything with Barcelona, titles with the senior national team eluded him. Within his beloved country, the criticism was fierce. His love for the jersey was questioned, his attitude, everything. It was even constantly criticized that “he didn’t sing the national anthem” before the start of the matches. And this was directed at him, who could have chosen an easier path elsewhere in the world. Yet he endured the scrutiny with grace, maintaining his composure and setting an example. Then came Brazil 2014. A World Cup on the soil of the “intimate enemy.” Argentina reached the final after 24 years. Everything seemed perfect; it was supposed to be the ultimate trophy. But Germany had other plans. Two more agonizing disappointments followed in consecutive Copa América finals against Chile. Messi hit rock bottom and gave up: “I’ve now lost four finals… My time with the national team is over. Four finals. It’s not for me. Unfortunately, I tried. It was what I wanted most. It didn’t happen for me, but I think that’s it.” But like a true champion, he reconsidered and quickly returned to the national squad. That period marked the most challenging stretch of his international career. After the lost finals, the team barely qualified for Russia 2018 and had a very poor showing. In 2019, he gave one of the most inspiring statements of his career. He made it clear on Fox Sports that he would not give up: “I want to finish my career having won something with the Argentina national team. And if not, at least having tried every possible time. That’s the message for the kids who follow me. Not just for soccer, but for life. Because that’s what life is: stumbling, getting back up, and trying again. Fighting for your dream.” Validation finally arrived at the 2021 Copa América in Brazil, where he lifted his first senior trophy 16 years after his debut. From that point on, the pressure lifted, allowing his genius to flow unburdened. At Qatar 2022, Messi captured the ultimate prize. The arduous journey to reach that moment made the triumph even sweeter. Fans rallied around his resilience, humility, and unwavering loyalty to his country. At 38, playing in his sixth World Cup, he proved decisive once again. In case there was any lingering doubt, he checked off another box that had always been brought up in comparisons with Maradona: he eliminated England, the great rival, with a brilliant performance. This time, his body didn’t allow him to play the final against Spain at his usual supersonic level. And the perfect ending wasn’t possible. But after this tournament, there was broad consensus that Messi stands as the greatest of all time. Argentine superstar Lionel Messi announced Monday that he is retiring from his country’s national team.“It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deep down — but I understand that the time has come,” he said in a statement on Instagram. “I swear to you that I always gave it my all — not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football.”Messi is widely considered to be one of the sport's all-time greatest players, and for many he is at the top of the list. He is Argentina's all-time leading goalscorer, and he led his country to a World Cup victory in 2022. At club level, he is the all-time leading scorer for FC Barcelona and the Spanish soccer league La Liga.Messi has won the Ballon d'Or trophy, given annually to the sport's top player, a record seven times. He has also won four Champions League titles with Barcelona. The captain’s eventual retirement from the national team came as no surprise. The death of his father weighed heavily on him, as reflected in his emotional farewell statemen: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you, I don’t know how to go on. I only played soccer and now I have serious doubts that I’ll keep doing it for much longer.” Besides, he’s 39 years old and time is starting to take its toll. Still, as obvious and expected as this farewell may have been, it doesn’t make it any less painful. There are unique and unrepeatable experiences in life. Sports lovers understand the privilege of seeing Michael Jordan, Roger Federer, or other GOATs live. It’s like watching a shooting star with a unique color pass through the vast sky, brighter than the rest, unrepeatable. His talent can still be appreciated in the MLS, although he has already given several hints that his time as a professional is coming to an end. Without a doubt, an era has ended—not only for Argentines, but for all soccer lovers. In his farewell post, Messi closes by writing, “Thank you God for making me Argentine.” Love for one’s country doesn’t depend on where you live. It depends on where you are from. And Messi is Argentine.

articles.title: Argentina president Javier Milei joins tributes to Messi, calls him an ‘impossible man’
articles.summary: Football News: Argentina's President Javier Milei honors Lionel Messi following the football star's retirement from international play, calling him an 'impossible man' and reflecting on his legendary career.
articles.body: Lionel Messi’s decision to end his international career has prompted an emotional reaction across Argentina, with President Javier Milei among those paying tribute to the captain who delivered some of the greatest moments in the country’s football history.Messi announced on Monday that he had decided to retire from international football following a period of reflection after Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The decision brought an end to a remarkable international career spanning six World Cups, 207 appearances and 125 goals for his country.Javier Milei pays tribute to Argentina’s captainArgentina President Javier Milei was among the first prominent figures to respond to Messi’s announcement.Sharing a photograph of the forward greeting supporters on Instagram, Milei wrote: “Muchas gracias HOMBRE IMPOSIBLE...!!!”The message roughly translates to: “Thank you very much, impossible man.”Milei’s tribute reflected the significance of Messi’s contribution to Argentine football, particularly after the forward helped end years of disappointment with the national team.Messi admitted the decision was painfulMessi’s announcement came more than a month after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium on July 19, a result that left the 39-year-old with another World Cup final defeat to add to his international story.The decision also arrived just weeks after Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, died on August 8 in Rosario at the age of 68, adding another deeply personal dimension to an already difficult period for the Argentina captain.Messi confirmed his international retirement through an emotional statement on Instagram, explaining that he had reached the point where he felt he had nothing more to give while also acknowledging the emergence of a younger generation within the national team.“After all this time since the final match, and after long reflection, I want to announce to everyone that I have decided to retire from playing with the national team,” Messi said.“It was a painful decision and it still hurts me deep down, but I realise that the time has come.”The Argentina captain stressed that his commitment to the national team had never wavered throughout his career, including during the years when major international success repeatedly eluded him.“I swear to you that I always gave everything I had, not only during the recent years in which we achieved everything, but before that too, and I always fought and gave all I had for this shirt, and to make you happy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football,” he added.Messi also acknowledged that the arrival of younger players had helped convince him that the time was right to step aside.“I have exhausted everything I have, and I no longer have any more to give, alongside the presence of a group of wonderful young players who deserve to get their chance,” he said.Messi’s Argentina career eventually became a story of redemptionMessi’s relationship with the Argentina national team was not always defined by the success that eventually came towards the end of his career.The forward suffered several major disappointments with his country, including defeat to Germany in the 2014 World Cup final and losses in consecutive Copa América finals before finally winning his first major senior international trophy at the 2021 Copa América.That triumph ended Argentina’s 28-year wait for a major international title and marked the beginning of an extraordinary period for Messi and his country.A year later, Messi captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar, beating France on penalties after a thrilling final finished 3-3 following extra time.Messi scored twice in that final and converted his penalty during the shootout, helping Argentina win the World Cup for the first time in 36 years and the third time in the country's history.He then helped Argentina retain the Copa América in 2024 before leading the team to another World Cup final in 2026, where Spain ultimately denied them back-to-back titles.Despite that final defeat, Messi leaves international football having achieved almost everything available to him with Argentina, including the World Cup, two Copa América titles and Olympic gold.Messi leaves behind an extraordinary World Cup recordMessi's longevity at international level is perhaps best illustrated by the fact that he appeared at six different World Cups between 2006 and 2026.Across those tournaments, he scored 21 goals in 34 appearances, placing him second on the all-time World Cup scoring list behind France captain Kylian Mbappé, who has moved ahead of him with 22 goals.Messi had previously overtaken Germany legend Miroslav Klose's tally before Mbappé eventually claimed the record.The 2026 tournament was another productive campaign for Messi individually, with the Argentina captain scoring eight goals and providing four assists.His performances included his first World Cup hat-trick, which came against Algeria during the tournament, further adding to a collection of records that had grown throughout his international career.By the time he announced his retirement, Messi had also established himself as Argentina's most-capped player and leading goalscorer, with 207 appearances and 125 goals according to the figures accompanying his retirement announcement.He also finishes as the highest-scoring player in South American international football.Messi will continue with Inter MiamiAlthough his international career is over, Messi has not announced his retirement from club football and will continue playing for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.The Argentine remains a central figure for the American club and underlined that status in spectacular fashion on August 30, scoring four goals and providing an assist for Luis Suárez in Inter Miami’s 7-1 victory over CF Montréal. Messi scored in the 40th, 52nd, 83rd and 90+6th minutes, completing his hat-trick with a chipped finish in the 83rd minute. The performance marked the 62nd hat-trick of his club career.Inter Miami currently sit fourth in the MLS standings with 42 points from 22 matches, having recorded 12 wins, six draws and four defeats, leaving them 10 points behind Nashville SC.For Argentina, however, a remarkable chapter has now closed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: Bukayo Saka earns win for the Gunners as they begin title defence with back-to-back victories
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Bukayo Saka's goal earned Arsenal a hard-fought 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park; Back-to-back wins for the Gunners to start their Premier League title defence while Unai Emery's side are still searching for their first point
articles.body:
This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Latest news and rumours: Aston Villa | Arsenal

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

Arsenal's talisman thought he had won a penalty early in the second half but Ian Maatsen's foul was ruled to be outside the box following a VAR review. It mattered not because he forced in Riccardo Calafiori's centre from close range soon afterwards.

The home side, who included debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson in their starting line-up, pushed for an equaliser but Arsenal, who brought on former Villa man Ezri Konsa late on, stayed strong to claim the win. A show of strength by the champions.

12 - BAR! Buendia lashes the ball against Raya's crossbar

56 - VAR! Saka denied penalty as Maatsen's foul is outside box

59 - GOAL! Calafiori's low cross is forced into the net by Saka

75 - MISS! Suzuki saves one-on-one from Havertz but he is off

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta speaking to Sky Sports:

"Really happy. A massive win. A tough place to come and earn the three points. We deserved it. A great squad performance - because when 11 wasn't enough the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to finish off the game.

"Last year we lost here in a really difficult way, with the last kick of the game. And that was still in the tummy.

"We are in the second game and it's like, 'we have to win this game!'

"We know that last year was the same. We know the level, we know how difficult it is for every team to earn points in this league, so we have to be really proud tonight."

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports:

"We've lost. We competed well. We are trying to rebuild the team but a lot of positive things after the result. How we compete defensively, with the ball. We didn't create clear chances but we didn't concede clear chances. It was so equal, the match.

"Some players made their debut, fantastic. Suzuki, Jackson both very good work. The first step forward, Today is positive for the next matches.

"To lose one match is painful but after we must try to get positive things. This is the reason I am being optimistic. There are 38 matches, we played two matches and didn't achieve points but hopefully we can get better."

Tzolis has made a promising start to his Arsenal career but this was a more difficult evening for him. The response from Arteta? Bring on Eze. He helped open it up for Arsenal to win. When Villa pushed, the Arsenal boss turned to Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino to battle it out.

"Guimaraes demonstrated already with a couple of passes he's going to be something very different to what they've already got," said Gary Neville on co-commentary for Sky Sports .

"He cuts through with his passing; he always looks for that furthest forward pass. Arsenal sometimes are guilty of recycling it too much - he won't do that."

But just as significant was how robust Arsenal looked in seeing this out. As well as the physical midfield trio, Konsa came on for Cristhian Mosquera. Villa did not even manage a shot on target. Rock solid.

With different players for different situations and back-to-back wins, the Gunners have already shown why they are still the team to beat in the Premier League. And they might just have got better.

As Premier League debuts go, replacing World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez for a game against the champions Arsenal right in front of the Holte End must be among the more daunting. Suzuki acquitted himself impressively for Aston Villa.

The Japan goalkeeper failed to claim one early cross but when he tipped over a near-post header soon after, the Villa fans were chanting 'the world's number one' - a playful reference to the popular chant that was traditionally directed at Martinez at Villa Park.

There was a little more lustre to the chant later in the first half when Suzuki pinged a pass out to George Hemmings on the left wing - arrowing the ball with extraordinary power. His distribution with both feet already looks likely to be a weapon for the team.

Suzuki did spill one fiercely struck shot in the second half but he denied Kai Havertz when one-on-one - not knowing that the offside flag would go up. Even in defeat, it was an encouraging showing by the new Villa goalkeeper.

articles.body: Hansi Flick ofreció su visión del cruce de este lunes contra el Rayo, correspondiente a la jornada 3 y disputado en el Spotify Camp Nou en el que el Barça se impuso por 5-2 a los madrileños. El técnico estaba contento por este triunfo que mantiene al Barcelona en lo más alto de la clasificación. "En la primera parte jugamos fantástico. Tuvimos una buena reacción al gol, es algo que podía ocurrir". "En casa tenemos que controlar mejor el partido. Tener más el balón. Es nuestra mentalidad, de algunos jugadores, ir arriba y atacar, pero a veces es necesario ralentizar el juego". "Rodri está aquí para controlar el partido en algunos momentos. Tiene que mejorar porque lleva pocos días con nosotros. Hay que controlar más porque el rival es muy bueno y tiene muchos jugadores que saben encontrar espacios. Y también son buenos a balón parado. "Gabriel es un delantero top. Nos puede aportar muchas cosas. Venía de lesión, y creo que está bien. Hablé con él, esta tarde. Estaba sorprendido. Me gusta, su estilo, cómo juega... encaja en nuestro estilo. Es un gran fichaje, Deco ha hecho un trabajo fantástico". "Lo importante son los tres puntos. Hemos empezado bien el curso. Jugamos muy bien la primera mitad contra el Rayo, reaccionamos bien tras el primer gol. Hay que mejorar en algunas fases... nuestro estilo requiere la recuperación del balón. Es más fácil recuperarse con el balón". "No sé si habrá más movimientos, no lo creo. Pero veremos. No lo creo". "Claro que me esperaba su rendimiento, es un futbolista de clase mundial. Lo quiero siempre en mi equipo. Y ser capitán es bueno para él. Hoy han pasado muchas cosas que me han puesto contento, algunos jugadores acaban de llegar y estar a gran nivel. Y el espíritu de equipo es fantástico. Hay que mejorar en algunas situaciones, y lo haremos". "Creo que él siempre quiere mejorar, y puede hacerlo. Estoy muy contento con él. Cómo juega... es increíble de ver. Está a un nivel increíble". "Es muy rápido, tiene buen manejo del balón. Hoy ha dado dos asistencias. Tenerle a él, a Karim, a Rapha, a Lamine... nos da mucha velocidad. Estoy muy contento con él".

articles.title: Luis de la Fuente encumbra a Rodrigo Hernández: "Es el Messi del fútbol español"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador español analiza el regreso de Rodri a LaLiga, la retirada internacional de Messi y las claves que utiliza para confeccionar sus convocatorias
articles.summary: El seleccionador español analiza el regreso de Rodri a LaLiga, la retirada internacional de Messi y las claves que utiliza para confeccionar sus convocatorias
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente fue el protagonista de la primera edición de ‘Otra Ronda’, el nuevo programa de Radio MARCA, donde repasó algunos de los asuntos de actualidad de la selección española y desveló parte de las claves que explican el éxito del equipo nacional en los últimos años. Uno de los nombres propios de la conversación fue Rodri, cuyo regreso a LaLiga considera una gran noticia para el fútbol español. El seleccionador no dudó en situar al centrocampista en lo más alto: “Rodri es el Messi del fútbol español”. De la Fuente considera que el jugador se adaptará a cualquier contexto porque “es el mejor del mundo en su posición”, aunque destacó especialmente el valor que tiene para el campeonato español que los grandes futbolistas nacionales vuelvan a competir en casa. “Celebro que estos grandes futbolistas estén en LaLiga, porque hace más grande la Liga. Hace verdaderamente que los mejores jugadores del mundo, que son nuestros futbolistas, estén compitiendo aquí en los clubes españoles”, explicó. En este sentido, reconoció que le gustaría que otros internacionales que todavía juegan en el extranjero también regresaran para demostrar su talento en el fútbol español. De la Fuente también tuvo palabras de admiración para Leo Messi, después de que el argentino haya puesto punto final a su etapa con la selección. El técnico español considera que todavía no somos capaces de valorar en su justa medida la dimensión de la carrera del argentino. “Es un personaje futbolístico que es de leyenda”, afirmó el seleccionador, que cree que será con el paso de los años cuando se tome verdadera perspectiva sobre sus logros. “Nos daremos cuenta de la dimensión futbolística de un jugador de fútbol que va a ser muy difícil que alguien supere los números que ha conseguido él”, señaló. Para De la Fuente, además, Messi todavía tiene recorrido por delante a nivel de clubes. “Él lo dejará cuando él quiera, no le dejará el fútbol a él”, apuntó. El seleccionador también explicó qué importancia tiene para él mantener una base de jugadores que se conocen y llevan tiempo trabajando juntos. La falta de tiempo durante las concentraciones convierte la continuidad en un elemento especialmente importante. “Nosotros tenemos el hándicap de que no tenemos mucho tiempo. No tenemos 38 jornadas ni diez jornadas para cambiar cosas que en la Liga se pueden hacer”, explicó. Por eso, considera fundamental construir un grupo sólido: “Con una buena convivencia, con un buen grupo, con una palabra equipo en mayúsculas, se camina mejor, más rápido, más seguro y más lejos”. Eso sí, De la Fuente dejó claro que la continuidad no está por encima del rendimiento deportivo. “La única motivación que tengo a la hora de tomar una decisión para convocar a un jugador es deportiva. No hay más motivaciones”, aseguró. El seleccionador insistió en que no mira el club de procedencia del futbolista y que sus decisiones responden exclusivamente a las necesidades deportivas de la selección y a los escenarios que puede plantear cada rival. “Con buena gente se viaja bien y con buenos futbolistas se compite todavía mejor”, resumió. Preguntado por si se imagina siendo seleccionador durante muchos años, De la Fuente evitó mirar demasiado lejos. “Soy muy cortoplacista en esto del fútbol”, reconoció. El técnico puso como ejemplo una conversación que mantuvo con varios jugadores justo después de ganar el Mundial. Mientras celebraban el título, algunos futbolistas le preguntaron qué les quedaba por ganar. Su respuesta fue inmediata: “De momento, el partido contra Inglaterra es de septiembre”. Una mentalidad que, según explicó, comparten también sus jugadores y que considera fundamental para mantener el hambre competitiva. “Quieren seguir compitiendo y ganando cosas”, destacó. Por eso, De la Fuente ya piensa en el siguiente reto y en la necesidad de evolucionar. “Vamos a seguir intentando mejorar todo, porque se puede mejorar”, afirmó. Y avisó de que cada nueva competición exige una versión diferente del equipo: “La próxima competición va a demandar otras cosas y va a ser tremendamente difícil. Nos va a exigir sacar todavía una nueva cara, una nueva versión”. Durante la entrevista también habló de su relación con los jugadores y de la importancia que concede al vestuario. El seleccionador definió al grupo como una familia y destacó que el respeto es una condición imprescindible para que la convivencia funcione. También dejó una reflexión sobre su manera de afrontar el día a día. Gran lector y aficionado a las reflexiones de filósofos y escritores, explicó que no se limita a seguir literalmente sus enseñanzas, sino que intenta adaptarlas a su propia vida. “Sobre todo cuando me dan luz para tomar decisiones en momentos determinados y me orientan en mi vida”, explicó. Una filosofía que traslada también al fútbol: trabajo, respeto, convivencia y rendimiento deportivo como pilares de una selección que, después de conquistar grandes títulos, ya prepara la siguiente versión de sí misma.

articles.title: Zabala lleva la locura a Las Gaunas en el minuto 92
articles.standfirst: El equipo azulgrana cae derrotado en el tiempo de descuento tras neutralizar Escudero el tanto inicial de la UD Logroñés en el minuto 72
articles.summary: El equipo azulgrana cae derrotado en el tiempo de descuento tras neutralizar Escudero el tanto inicial de la UD Logroñés en el minuto 72
articles.body: La Primera Federación arrancó su curso 26/27 con un pequeño clásico del Grupo 1 y con un guion que se resolvió en el último suspiro. La UD Logroñés se impuso 2-1 al CD Extremadura ante 4.431 espectadores gracias a un tanto de Mikel Zabala en el minuto 90, un desenlace que premió la insistencia local y castigó a un rival que se había ganado el empate a base de reacción. Fue un partido de emociones tardías, de banquillos decisivos y de un final que dejó a los riojanos con un botín de tres puntos que, por cómo se pusieron las cosas, saben todavía más. FICHA TÉCNICA UD LOGROÑÉS: Fermín; Navarro, Bolo, Cabetas, Camacho, Marí, Latif (Maroto, min. 75), Santana (Chinedu, min. 75), Asenjo (Zabala, min. 63), Anai y Baselga (Amigo, min. 75). EXTREMADURA: Alfonso; Barace (Ismael, min. 76), Correa, Cordero, Macías, Chus Villar (Iker, min. 87), Zarfino. Luis Nicolás (Yael, min. 75), Diego, Kike Márquez (Escudero, min. 58) y Manchón Goles 1-0: Baselga, min. 14. 1-1: Escudero, min. 72. 2-1: Zabala, min. 92. Árbitro Marc Oltra (catalán). Ayudado por Martín y Melón. Amonestó a los blanquirrojos Latif, Camacho, Santana y Bolo; y los extremeños Cordero y Escudero. Incidencias Las Gaunas, 4.431 espectadores. Iñaki Sáenz realizó el saque de honor. También se rindió homenaje a Ceuta bajo el lema 'Ceuta no se vende. Ceuta se defiende'. Un guion de tres actos El encuentro tuvo un arranque nervioso. Antes del cuarto de hora, la UD Logroñés ya acumulaba dos amonestaciones —Latif Issman al minuto 8 y Sergio Camacho al 11—, señal de un choque de alta fricción desde el pitido inicial. Pero lejos de resentirse, fueron los locales quienes golpearon primero: en el minuto 15, Marcos Baselga culminó una jugada asistida por Ismael Santana para poner el 1-0 y calmar los ánimos de la afición riojana. Con la renta a favor, la UD Logroñés se marchó al descanso por delante. El segundo acto, sin embargo, cambió de dueño. El CD Extremadura reaccionó con los cambios: Rodrigo Escudero, que había entrado al campo en el minuto 59 en el lugar de Kike Márquez, encontró premio en el 74 al rematar un centro de Imanol Barace para firmar el 1-1. El empate era justo por la valentía visitante en la segunda mitad y ponía al equipo extremeño en la senda de un debut con premio. El tercer acto, no obstante, lo escribió el banquillo local. La UD Logroñés había movido su once en bloque en el minuto 76, dando entrada a Mario Maroto, David Amigo y Prince Chinedu, además del ya presente Zabala, que había ingresado en el 63. Y fue precisamente el eje Chinedu-Zabala el que decidió el partido: en el minuto 90, Chinedu asistió a Mikel Zabala para el 2-1 definitivo. Un desenlace de manual sobre cómo un cuerpo técnico puede reescribir un partido desde la revolución de piezas. Las claves del duelo El desarrollo del choque dejó una lectura clara sobre el acierto en la gestión de los cambios. Los tres goles del encuentro llevaron firma de asistencia —Santana, Barace y Chinedu—, lo que refleja un partido de acciones elaboradas más que de individualidades sueltas. La UD Logroñés supo mantener la calma tras encajar el empate en un momento delicado y encontró recompensa en el descuento, mientras que el CD Extremadura pagó caro no haber cerrado el partido en los instantes en los que dominó la iniciativa tras su gol. La tarjeta que vio Rodrigo Escudero en el minuto 84, apenas diez minutos después de convertirse en héroe momentáneo del cuadro visitante, ilustra bien la tensión de un tramo final en el que el Extremadura se vio superado por el empuje local. La UD Logroñés cerró el partido con una última amonestación, la de Taliby Konate en el 90, ya con el resultado sentenciado. Cómo queda la clasificación En una primera jornada en la que todo está por definir, la victoria coloca a la UD Logroñés en la tercera posición del Grupo 1, con tres puntos y un balance de un partido ganado, gracias a su diferencia de goles (+1) tras el 2-1. Por encima quedan únicamente el Real Unión Club, líder con un contundente 4-1, y el CD Lugo, segundo tras vencer por 3-1. Todos ellos comparten los tres puntos, pero la mayor cantidad de goles a favor de los dos primeros les otorga la ventaja en el desempate inicial. El reverso de la moneda lo vive el CD Extremadura, que arranca el curso en la decimocuarta plaza con cero puntos y una derrota que le deja con un gol a favor y dos en contra. No es un desenlace dramático a estas alturas —una sola jornada apenas dibuja tendencias—, pero sí un aviso: el equipo visitante mereció más por su reacción y se marchó de vacío por detalles del tramo final. El grupo se completa por abajo con conjuntos como el CD Coria, que encajó cuatro goles en su debut, o el Unionistas de Salamanca CF, que cayó por 3-1. Jugadores a seguir El nombre de la jornada en el bando local es, sin discusión, Mikel Zabala. Su irrupción desde el banquillo y su gol en el minuto 90 le convierten en el hombre que decidió el partido, la clase de futbolista que un entrenador agradece tener como revulsivo. A su lado, Prince Chinedu merece mención por partida doble: entró en el 76 y catorce minutos después ya había repartido la asistencia del triunfo. En el CD Extremadura, Rodrigo Escudero dejó la mejor imagen individual pese a la derrota. Su gol en el 74, también desde el banquillo, mantuvo con vida a los suyos y confirmó su condición de recurso ofensivo a tener muy presente en las próximas jornadas. Lo que viene La primera lectura del curso invita al optimismo en Logroño: un triunfo trabajado, sufrido y resuelto en el descuento es de esos que fortalecen a un vestuario desde el primer día. El CD Extremadura, en cambio, tendrá que transformar en puntos el buen fondo de juego que exhibió en la segunda mitad. En una categoría tan igualada como la Primera Federación, donde los márgenes son mínimos y un gol en el 90' cambia una clasificación entera, saber competir hasta el último segundo será, como quedó demostrado en este estreno, la diferencia entre sumar y lamentar.

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki, Joao Pedro, Bruno Fernandes
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (Hull City): Again, another massive performance, another clean sheet. Hull have taken everyone by surprise, but it's because of that defensive shape and defensive organisation, and obviously, he is at the heart of that as well.

Semi Ajayi (Hull City): Coming up with Hull is the only way he was going to ever play in the Premier League. He has been doing the rounds in the Championship for years. A real good solid pro. He has taken this opportunity and he's been an absolute beast, so fair play to him.

Nordi Mukiele (Sunderland): He was great last season, a real, real powerful centre-half. Again, a top performance from him. Fulham had no shots on target - he was a massive part of that.

James Tarkowski (Everton): It was a captain's performance for Everton. Just one of those guys that you want in your team. No-one ever respects him, no-one ever rates him, but when you play against him and when he's in your team, he's a real bloke. Proper captain, proper leader of men, and kept going right to the end. And ultimately, even though the two Bournemouth defenders decided to mark themselves, he was the one who got the goal.

James McAtee (Nottingham Forest): He absolutely ran the game at Anfield from start to finish. Getting on the ball in the pockets, half-turn, playing forward. He was the reason they were any good, and he's very, very good, but won't be spoken about in the same breath as the goalscorers.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United): There's not much more to say. Captain Fantastic, three goals, an assist, and nearly scored from the halfway line. Where would Manchester United be without him? Relegated is the answer.

Rayan Cherki (Manchester City): My favourite player in world football to watch. Amazing the way he's gifted with the ball, the way he manipulates the ball, and also the way he's able to think for himself. And I just like the fact he's carefree. He just wants to play football, so that's great.

Anthony Elanga (Newcastle): Back-to-back weeks, another great goal, another great performance. Just looks like he's had another lease of life under this manager. And I wonder whether we're going to see the Elanga that we saw at Nottingham Forest, just terrorising defences with that pace. But also, before he even gets there, they're just worried about what he can do.

Yoane Wissa (Newcastle): I had to shoehorn him in because ultimately he's been great through the middle, but the two strikers have actually scored more and played better than him. But Wissa's a massive part of why Newcastle have done well, although he's not being talked about enough in terms of the application that he puts in. So much so, that Woltemade could be sold. That's how much of a good job Wissa has done.

Joao Pedro (Chelsea): He has had an unbelievable start to the season. I think under Xabi Alonso, and with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers behind him, he's going to have an unbelievable season. But also the fact that he wasn't even picked for the World Cup. Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti was there, and Joao Pedro looks like he has a point to prove.

Erling Haaland (Manchester City): The beast, the Viking, the new haircut. Two goals, comfortable. Just looks like actually playing football is too easy for him. He looks like scoring goals is just becoming a bit boring and he's probably trying to think of ways to do it better.

Matthias Jaissle (Newcastle): What a start to the season he's had. Also, the demeanour he gives off is young Jose Mourinho vibes. Very Jose at Porto, without saying he's the Special One. Calm, confident, a little bit arrogant at times, but also just looks like you want to play for him. Looks like he knows what he's talking about.

articles.title: UCLA Fires AD amid 'Significant Financial Deficit,' Replaced by Former Lakers Exec Tim Harris
articles.summary: UCLA is moving on from athletic director Martin Jarmond after more than five years at the helm, per ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
UCLA is moving on from athletic director Martin Jarmond after more than five years at the helm, per ESPN's Pete Thamel .

The school is replacing Jarmond with former Los Angeles Lakers executive Tim Harris, who will work the interim role on a pro bono basis.

Jarmond's firing comes amid what UCLA described as a "significant financial deficit."

"UCLA Athletics currently carries a significant financial deficit, and its current path is not sustainable," UCLA Chancellor Julio Frenk wrote in a statement. "Now is the moment to build a model for Athletics that protects the breadth of our program, creates new opportunities for student-athletes and coaches, and supports itself through the revenue it generates.

"I believe UCLA should help lead the transformation of intercollegiate athletics: our future must be shaped by purpose — not by pressure."

Since Jarmond took over in 2020, UCLA's major sports have struggled to find much success, primarily in football. The Bruins have reached just three bowl games and are coming off a 3-9 season.

UCLA basketball reached the Final Four in Jarmond's first year as AD but hasn't made it past the Sweet 16 since then. Its women's team has found more success, reaching the Elite Eight two years ago and the Final Four last year.

But Jarmond's firing seemingly has more to do with what has happened off the field. According to Ben Bolch of the California Post , UCLA has been in the red in every fiscal year since Jarmond took over and ran up a tab of $241.1 million, requiring a university bailout.

Frenk also cited UCLA's struggles in the NIL department in his letter announcing Jarmond's firing.

"We have all watched as the landscape of college athletics has transformed in recent years, driven by the introduction of Name, Image and Likeness (NIL), new models for student-athlete compensation and a rapidly changing sports marketplace," Frenk wrote. "UCLA must have an athletics model that leads — not just keeps pace."

UCLA will now begin a search for its next athletics director, but will be led by Harris in the meantime.

Harris was a goalkeeper for UCLA's soccer team in the 1980s and went on to forge a 35-year career with the Lakers, where he served as president of business operations.

"Simply put, he loves UCLA and cares deeply about our future," Frenk wrote of Harris. "Tim knows what it takes to grow a world-class sports organization and global brand, and he holds longstanding relationships throughout Los Angeles and globally. He brings decades of experience in creating partnerships and new sources of revenue, along with a personal focus on centering the student-athlete experience. I am especially grateful for Tim's willingness to serve UCLA on a pro bono basis.

"Tim will develop a new strategy to grow revenue through partnerships, licensing and other ventures, while ensuring that our student-athletes and coaches have the required support to compete at the highest level."

UCLA football begins its football season on Saturday against Cal, marking the start of the Bob Chesney era after the head coach was hired in December.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta: Arsenal boss joins elite list of managers, but where does he rank?
articles.summary: At full-time in Arsenal's 1-0 win at Aston Villa, the travelling supporters sang about how their team will win the league again with Mikel Arteta in charge.
articles.body:
When thinking of the greatest managers of the Premier League era, Arsene Wenger, Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola are names that belong high on the list.

They are three of the rare breed to have managed 250 games with a single Premier League club, and Mikel Arteta is now the 10th member of that elite group.

Monday's 1-0 win over Aston Villa was the 250th top-flight game in charge for Arteta with the Gunners, and his champions delivered a trademark performance.

At full-time at Villa Park, the travelling supporters sang about how they are going to win the league again with Arteta in charge.

With Arsenal coming into this season as trophy holders, and with transition affecting rivals Liverpool , Manchester City , Chelsea and Manchester United , it is hard to see how the fans' partisan prediction is going to be proved wrong.

Arsenal conceded the fewest goals in the league last season as they won the title for the first time in 22 years.

And during Arteta's nearly seven years in charge, the Gunners have become renowned for their defensive excellence.

Against Aston Villa they showed it again, without allowing a shot on target against them as Bukayo Saka's second-half goal secured victory.

The latest win not only puts Arteta in the 250 club. He also has the fourth-best win percentage among those bosses, with only Guardiola, Ferguson and Jurgen Klopp ahead of him.

Arteta is the longest-serving current Premier League manager and with his longevity has come an Arsenal identity.

Arsenal have become renowned for being difficult to break down and new players repeatedly say that they are impressed and sometimes overwhelmed by the level of detail coming from Arteta.

This is the fifth season in a row where Arsenal have won their first two Premier League matches and they again have a solid platform to build another title challenge.

The Gunners have only faced three shots on target in their first two Premier League games. Villa drew a blank in that regard.

During their title triumph last season, the Gunners did not allow their opponents a shot on target in six league matches, the joint-most of any side in a campaign on record since the 2003-04 season.

Goalkeeper David Raya has won the the Golden Glove award for the most clean sheets in each of the past three seasons, while William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes have been voted in the PFA team of the year for the past three seasons too.

Since the start of March, the Gunners have kept eight Premier League clean sheets – three more than any other side and the only side in Europe's big-five leagues to have kept more are Juventus with nine.

"It's how they defend as a team and how they attack as a team," Arsenal 's record goalscorer Thierry Henry told Sky Sports after the game.

"One thing is sure with Arsenal - everybody needs to run. You don't have any passengers in that team. This is how you win a title. You can see they are so good at it."

Saka scores only goal as Arsenal beat Villa

How did match-winner Saka do? Aston Villa v Arsenal ratings

Arteta builds on firm foundations - still business to be done?

Arsenal have one of the best squads in Europe.

The Gunners spent £250m last summer bringing in eight players as they won the title and have already spent about £200m this year, turning Piero Hincapie's loan deal into a permanent one (£34.5m), signing Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United (£75m), Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge (£34m) and bringing in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa (£55m).

"That is what we need," Arteta said, speaking to Sky Sports when asked about his squad depth.

"The players that come in make the difference. All of them contributed to create more dominance and more momentum.

"The level of focus and the way they want to contribute to the team, that is going to be decisive in the season."

Arsenal 's strength in depth cannot be understated, but one area they may still look to strengthen in is the forward area.

The Gunners have been on the hunt for an elite forward to lift their attack and still could be active on Tuesday's deadline day.

They had an unsuccessful pursuit of Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr, while they also have a long-standing interest in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez.

"We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we will try to do it," Arteta said.

"I have been disconnected from the world for the last 24 hours because my energy has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now."

When pushed about a deal for Alvarez, Arteta said: "I don't know, that's for the people upstairs."

Whatever happens in Arsenal 's search, they are going to be hard to keep off the top of the table with Arteta at the helm.

articles.title: UCLA fires AD Martin Jarmond after struggles, financial issues just days before Bob Chesney's Bruins debut
articles.summary: UCLA is bringing in a former Lakers executive to be the interim athletic director on a pro bono basis.
articles.body:
Martin Jarmond is out at UCLA, and new head football coach Bob Chesney is set to have a new boss days before taking the field for the first time running the program.

UCLA fired Jarmond as its athletic director on Monday, the school announced. Jarmond had been with the Bruins since 2020, and is set to be owned $6.5 million that is left on his contract with the university, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel . He signed a five-year extension with UCLA in 2024.

Tim Harris will serve as the CEO and athletic director for the program on an interim basis. The former Lakers executive will do that on a pro bono basis, too.

UCLA chancellor Julio Frenk announced the move in a message to the university on Monday afternoon.

"We have all watched as the landscape of college athletics has transformed in recent years, driven by the introduction of Name, Image and Likeness (NIL), new models for student-athlete compensation and a rapidly changing sports marketplace," Frenk said, in part. "UCLA must have an athletics model that leads — not just keeps pace."

UCLA football has struggled to find real relevance in recent years, and didn't even last two full seasons under head coach DeShaun Foster. The Bruins fired Foster after the team lost three straight games to open the 2025 campaign. Foster was meant to be the replacement for Chip Kelly, too, after Kelly left for an assistant job at Ohio State.

UCLA then hired Chesney, who will officially make his debut with the school on Saturday in their season opener at California (10:30 p.m. ET, ESPN) after his dominant run with James Madison.

Jarmond was hired to replace Dan Guerrero in 2020. The Bruins have won nine national championships under his watch, including when UCLA women's basketball went 37-1 and won the NCAA tournament earlier this spring.

But perhaps the biggest issue has been financial. According to the California Post , UCLA's athletic department ran a deficit of $21.6 million during the fiscal year ending in June 2025. That was down nearly $30 million from the previous year, too. The school has run a deficit in every year under Jarmond's watch, and ran up a tab of more than $241 million. The university had to come in and offer the athletic department a bailout after the end of the 2024 fiscal year.

UCLA officially joined the Big Ten in 2024, a move that should help relieve some financial strain in the years to come due to the league's media rights deals. Travel costs are up, too. Rutgers, the furthest Big Ten school from UCLA, is some 2,800 miles away.

"UCLA Athletics currently carries a significant financial deficit, and its current path is not sustainable," Frenk said. "Now is the moment to build a model for Athletics that protects the breadth of our program, creates new opportunities for student-athletes and coaches, and supports itself through the revenue it generates. "I believe UCLA should help lead the transformation of intercollegiate athletics: Our future must be shaped by purpose — not by pressure."

While there were undoubtedly some successes, failing to revive a football program and running a constant financial deficit are major issues that the university decided it could no longer overlook.

Who ends up leading UCLA athletics long term remains to be seen. But for now, it'll be Harris' job to oversee the beginning of the Chesney era and start the process of turning the once-dominant Southern California sports school around.

articles.title: Folarin Balogun to Everton in New Transfer Rumors as USMNT Star Agrees to Contract with EPL Club
articles.summary: Folarin Balogun is heading back to England.
articles.body:
Folarin Balogun is heading back to England.

Everton have reportedly agreed on a transfer fee with Monaco to bring aboard the USMNT striker and former Arsenal man ahead of Tuesday's transfer deadline, per Patrick Boyland, James Horncastle and Tom Bogert of The Athletic .

Per that report, "Monaco sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, stated a deal consisting of an initial €45 million (£38.58 million; $52.3 million) plus €5 million (£4.3 million; $5.8 million) in potential add-ons had been agreed between the two clubs, while Everton sources said the deal was worth in the region of £40 million ($54 million; €46.7 million)."

Football reporter Fabrizio Romano reported later on Monday that Balogun has agreed on personal terms with Everton.

Balogun, 25, scored 13 goals and added four assists for Monaco in France's Ligue 1 last season, by far his best campaign with the club after joining from Arsenal in the 2022-23 campaign.

And he was brilliant for the United States in the World Cup ( red card controversies aside ), scoring three goals in four games. Now he'll be returning to the Premier League as a part of Everton's revamped attack after the club also reportedly agreed to bring back Jack Grealish on a season-long loan and reportedly came to an agreement to sell winger Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City.

Tyrique George and Brennan Johnson have also been added out wide this summer.
